Why Brewer

Everything brew does, one click away

No mystery. Each button runs the exact brew command you would have typed - and shows you its output while it runs.

Updates

See what's outdated. Upgrade it your way.

133 packages behind? Upgrade everything, cherry-pick one, or snooze the noisy ones for a week.

  • Scheduled checks with notifications - every 6h, daily, or weekly
  • Automatic background upgrades that wait for AC power
  • Running apps are closed cleanly before their upgrade
  • The menu bar icon shows the outdated count at a glance
Live console

Watch Homebrew do its thing

A Cakebrew-style console docks at the bottom of the window. Install something and the real output streams in - colors, warnings, exit codes, a Stop button.

  • Every operation is queued and logged; failed ones keep their output in History
  • Readable brew doctor, cleanup previews with sizes
  • Failures show the real error - not a shrug
Beyond Homebrew

Every app on your Mac, one inventory

Brewer scans everything - casks, App Store buys, Sparkle self-updaters, and apps you dragged in years ago - with size, source, and architecture.

  • Update Sparkle apps directly: download, back up the old version, install
  • Read the release notes before you say yes
  • Roll back from automatic backups if a new version misbehaves
  • Setapp and App Store editions stay with their own stores, so licenses never break
  • Adopt manually-installed apps so brew manages them from now on
Uninstaller

Delete apps without the crumbs

Drop any app on Brewer and it finds the caches, preferences, containers and logs left behind - then trashes it all together. Casks go through brew, leftovers included.

  • Everything goes to the Trash, so nothing is lost forever
  • SmartDelete notices when you delete an app and offers to clean up after it
  • System and Apple apps are protected - always
Why Brewer

Homebrew has its own window now. Brewer looks after the whole Mac.

Homebrew 7 ships BrewUI, an official app for browsing and searching packages on macOS 26 and later. Brewer is built for everything around the packages, and it runs on macOS 14 Sonoma and later.

  • Mac App Store and Sparkle app updates next to Homebrew's, with release notes and backups
  • Uninstalls that take caches, preferences and containers with them
  • Scheduled, battery-aware upgrades with a menu bar counter
  • A health score, structured brew doctor findings and brew vulns security advisories
  • Tap trust per installed package, and packages from untrusted taps stay in view
  • Services, taps, Brewfiles, app adoption and a history of every command

And the rest

Small features you'll end up using daily

🔎

Search everything

Formulae, casks and third-party taps from one bar. Paste owner/tap/pkg and Brewer adds the missing tap for you, while Homebrew trusts just that package.

🧾

Know before you install

Dependencies, license, caveats, disk usage and quarantine status - before anything touches your system.

⚙️

Services

Start, stop and restart brew services - databases and daemons - without touching launchctl.

📦

Brewfile

Export your whole setup to a Brewfile, or replay one on a new Mac. Moving machines takes minutes.

🩺

Health dashboard

Outdated counts, deprecated packages, orphans, cache size, doctor findings and known vulnerabilities - scored at a glance.

🧹

Cleanup

Preview exactly what brew cleanup would delete, file by file with sizes, then reclaim the space.

🏷️

Tags & collections

Favorites, pins, per-package notes, tags and collections - organize a big setup your way.

🍏

Apple Silicon scan

Find apps still running under Rosetta 2 and Homebrew installs living in the wrong prefix.

🛍️

App Store too

With the mas CLI, Mac App Store apps join the same update flow - one place for everything.
